I am a PhD student in the Department of Political Science at the University of California San Diego.

I study comparative politics and the political economy of development, with a regional focus on Turkey, MENA, and Southeastern Europe. My current research examines how governments build electoral support through distributive programs, including social assistance, subsidized public services, and credit. I also work on the historical political economy of state building in the late Ottoman Empire. My empirical work centers on causal inference, combining quasi-experimental designs for observational data, experimental methods, and geospatial analysis, alongside LLM-based archival data extraction. I am also developing a specialization in formal theory.
